Slow Reading in a Fast World

The pace of new information has not slowed for years, even as our attention has become more fragmented across many different devices and apps every day.

Slow reading is a small rebellion. It says that the value of a sentence depends on whether your mind has time to actually meet it, not just sweep past it.

When you give a paragraph a few seconds longer than it strictly needs, you discover that meaning compounds. The next paragraph rests on the previous one and the writer's argument finally reaches you.

Speed reading tools should serve this goal. The point is not to finish faster but to keep your eyes steady so your mind can do the harder work of understanding without distraction.
